name: Tarotop
tagline: An AI companion app that remembers your history and frames conversations as tarot readings.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The ingredients here are unusually public: the 78 card Rider-Waite deck, its imagery, and its standard upright and reversed meanings are all out of copyright and well documented. Everything else is an LLM with a persona prompt, a shuffle function, and a database that stores your past readings so the companion can refer back to them. A coding agent can assemble that in one sitting, and the result is arguably better because you control the persona and nothing is rate limited behind a subscription tier. What you cannot one-shot is the part people actually pay for: art direction, a companion that feels like a character rather than a chatbot in a robe, and the push notification that nudges you at 9am. If the reading is the point, build it. If the relationship with a specific designed character is the point, you are not rebuilding that in an afternoon.
coreLoopDIY: Shuffles a public domain 78 card deck into a chosen spread, then has a persona-locked LLM interpret the draw in the context of your stored past readings and notes.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local model via Ollama)
Public domain Rider-Waite card scans, or plain text cards if you skip art
Somewhere to run it: localhost is fine, a small VPS if you want it on your phone browser
whatYouLose: A real mobile app with push notifications and offline access
Designed character art and card illustrations that look intentional rather than scraped
Persona tuning that someone iterated on with real users, instead of your first draft system prompt
Memory that actually summarizes and surfaces the right past reading, which is harder than appending rows to a table
Any sense that the companion exists independently of you, which is most of the appeal for most users
moatNotes: Divination apps live and die on vibe. The retrieval is trivial; making a character that people want to talk to twice is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because this is an emotional product, not a utility. Nobody opens a tarot app to retrieve card meanings they could have looked up in thirty seconds; they open it because the thing on the other side feels like a presence that knows them. That feeling comes from art, pacing, voice, and the accumulated weight of months of logged readings, and a self-built clone starts at zero on all four. There is also the quiet switching cost of history: once a year of readings and journal entries live inside someone's companion, a blank new one feels like a stranger.
notes: The deck is public domain, which makes this one of the rare AI companion apps whose entire content layer is free to copy.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI tarot companion web app. Stack: Next.js 14 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, and SQLite via better-sqlite3. No auth, no cloud, no telemetry, single user on localhost.

Data:
1. Seed a JSON file with all 78 Rider-Waite-Smith cards: name, arcana, suit, number, keywords, upright meaning, reversed meaning. Write real meanings, not placeholders.
2. SQLite tables: readings (id, created_at, spread, question, drawn_cards JSON, interpretation), notes (id, reading_id, body, created_at), memory (id, kind, body, created_at) for rolled-up summaries about the user.

Core loop:
3. Home page: a question box, a spread picker (single card, three card past/present/future, Celtic Cross), and a Draw button.
4. On draw, shuffle server-side with crypto randomness, pick cards, randomly set reversed at 30 percent per card, persist the draw before any model call.
5. Call an LLM (OpenAI by default, base URL and model from .env, key in .env only, never hardcoded) with: a persona system prompt for a calm, slightly wry familiar; the drawn cards and orientations; the question; and the 10 most recent memory rows.
6. Stream the interpretation into the page. Reveal cards one at a time with a short CSS flip before the text starts.
7. After each reading, make a second cheap model call that extracts at most two durable facts about the user and inserts them into memory. Dedupe by fuzzy string match.

Also build:
8. A /journal page listing past readings with date, spread, cards, and a free text note field per reading.
9. A /memory page that lists memory rows and lets me delete or edit any of them. This must be fully user-editable.
10. A single persona file at /lib/persona.ts with the system prompt in one exported string so I can rewrite the character without touching logic.

Out of scope: user accounts, payments, mobile app, push notifications, card artwork (render cards as styled typographic placeholders with the card name and a CSS border, and read optional images from /public/cards/{slug}.jpg if present).

Deliver: npm install, npm run dev, and a README with .env.example, the schema, and one paragraph on how to swap in a local Ollama model.
